page.layout: One page of text in one column. In the middle is a syllogism figure: a column of premises and conclusion on the left, and boxes with a brace and letters A, B, C on the right. Below it come two short italic example syllogisms. No margin notes. Top right: page number 299. Running head: LIBER IIII.

main_text.p: In hac autem figura hoc perpetuum est, ut nulla ex ea colligi affirmatio possit.

Quomodo medium sub utroque extremo collocatur? Cùm de Mediũ utrunque extremum pronuntiatur. Cùm & in propositione & in assumptione Mediũ utriusque extremi subiectum est, veluti, Ponatur quæstio, An aliqui homines sint atri, deinde sumatur Mediũ ex specie: nimirum, Aethiopes.
Huius autem figurae hoc proprium est, ut con-clusio semper sit particularis, veluti,

Possumusne, quoniam hæ Figurae appellantur, & ex Mathematicorum consuetudine sumptę sunt, descriptionem earum aliquam ob oculos ponere? Licet vero, idque Aristotelis exemplo, qui cum adolescentibus in mathematicis artibus eruditis Logicam traderet, accuratè istam figurarum & descriptionum consuetudinem seruauit.

page.notes: The syllogism figure has braces, which are drawn and not printed text. The letters A, B, C are labels beside the boxes, and I have put them after the box with a bar. The left column of premises and the right column of boxes share the same lines, so the row order is approximate. The long s is rendered as s throughout, and u/v and i/j are normalised as the rules require. The tilde in "Mediũ" is kept as printed. No catchword, signature or margin notes are visible.
